A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VX-CODE study. Their main texts and complete supplementary materials contain readable equations, tables, figures, and experimental descriptions that support comparison across reorganized sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative and qualitative evaluations of VX-CODE, including benchmark comparisons, computational ablations, synthetic-bias experiments, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds failure-case evaluations, comparisons with VPS and Monte Carlo Shapley estimates, and masking and weight-randomization tests.

M1.justification: The core reward, greedy insertion/deletion, patch selection, and step restriction remain. However, the documented rule restricting eligible patches changes: v1 Appendix B.8 applies it when Rbox <= 0.1 with margins w/5 and h/5; v2 Appendix C.7 uses Rbox <= 0.2 and margins w/7 and h/7. This changes the explanation search region. The new π*-index provides theoretical interpretation rather than a new selection algorithm.

E1.justification: MS-COCO, PASCAL VOC, and the seven-class synthetic marker dataset are retained. v2 adds dedicated misclassification and mislocalization test scenarios, extending coverage to explaining naturally occurring detector failures. Grounding DINO is evaluated on MS-COCO; its addition alone does not establish a new dataset or open-vocabulary task.

E2.justification: v2 adds two directly relevant comparator families: Monte Carlo estimated Shapley values in Appendix D.2 and the greedy-search method VPS in Section 5.5 and Appendix D.13. VPS is evaluated with Grounding DINO, DETR, and Faster R-CNN. The original six baselines remain in Table 1; BSED and FSOD remain citations rather than reported evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include 200 detections per failure type, Grounding DINO evaluation on 100 instances above confidence 0.6, and VPS comparisons on 500 instances above 0.7. v2 also adds a 200-sample Monte Carlo baseline evaluated on 100 detections, weight-randomization checks using SSIM and rank correlation, and blur-versus-zero masking. The search-window settings are explicitly revised, but the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds masking-sensitivity tests, model-weight randomization sanity checks, and quantitative and qualitative analyses of misclassification and mislocalization. It also expands the existing weighted-reward analysis to additional examples and patch deletion. The original patch-combination, computational ablation, biased-model, and detector-comparison analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for experimental results. The new Monte Carlo sampling budget describes how a comparator estimates feature contributions, rather than uncertainty reporting or repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but v2 adds substantial failure-case, VPS, Monte Carlo, masking, and randomization results. For example, its Grounding DINO comparison reports overall AUC 0.751 for VX-CODE versus 0.646 for VPS. Retained pointing-game results are also revised: insertion PG(M) changes from 0.953 to 0.905, EPG(B) from 0.644 to 0.520, and EPG(M) from 0.443 to 0.351 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6). These revisions do not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the π*-index, an optimal ordering objective, and a sequential coalitional-game interpretation in Section 4.3. Appendix C.8 adds the elimination variant and arguments concerning null-player, linearity, and efficiency properties, while excluding symmetry. It also revises the accelerated complexity expression to include the early-step factor γn/r. These additions substantially extend v1's self-context and full-context derivations.

C1.justification: The central claim that collective contributions improve detector explanations is retained. However, v2 adds the π*-index and its asserted axiomatic properties as a principal contribution, and reframes efficient computation of Shapley quantities as their incorporation through a heuristic. It also claims novelty in analyzing greedy patch selection through game-theoretic indices, substantially changing the stated theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly distinguishes the method's goal from accurate Shapley approximation, leaves approximation analysis and reward design unresolved, and discusses evaluation validity. Section 4.3 acknowledges that greedy ordering need not recover the optimal ordering. v2 also adds redundancy-based interaction explanations and interpretations of detector failures through background correlations. Existing pointing-game limitations and insertion-versus-deletion interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.6 newly explains how patches selected together for r >= 2 receive individual reward values: their ordering is chosen by examining r! permutations. Appendix C.7 revises the documented search-window parameters. These improve or change implementation documentation without establishing that the newly explained ordering procedure was introduced in v2. Both versions still promise future code release.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against SAG, REX, VPS, and logic-based explanation approaches, alongside new references supporting masking, error diagnosis, and sanity checks. Section 2 and Appendix B distinguish the contribution through game-theoretic analysis of patch search and sequential coalitional games. This goes beyond v1's positioning primarily as an extension of MoXI to object detection.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries become a separate section, biased-model examples move into the motivation, detailed bounding-box evaluation moves to the appendix, and the supplementary material is reorganized around limitations, related work, method details, and experiments. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond renumbering or adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the method overview, compacts and relocates the opening illustration, and adds performance curves, failure-case panels, and new comparison tables. It merges the former aeroplane bias table into a broader appendix table and expands the weighted-reward figure. Several existing visualization grids are preserved and relocated, rather than constituting new results.

improvement.justification: The added masking and weight-randomization checks, direct VPS and Monte Carlo comparisons, and clearer limitations strengthen empirical credibility beyond v1. However, the new linearity argument in Appendix C.8 holds π* fixed across reward functions although Definition 5 makes its optimum reward-dependent, leaving a prominent theoretical claim unsupported. The empirical and documentation gains support a limited net improvement despite this theoretical gap.
